relationships.description: Links an account-association record to the Saviynt user who owns or is associated with the account.
relationships.evidence: Observed directly in existing Saviynt analytics SQL: users.USERKEY = user_accounts.USERKEY.

relationships.description: Links a user-account association to the corresponding account record.
relationships.evidence: Observed directly in existing Saviynt analytics SQL: user_accounts.ACCOUNTKEY = accounts.ACCOUNTKEY.

relationships.description: Links an account to the endpoint on which the account exists.
relationships.evidence: Observed directly in existing Saviynt analytics SQL: accounts.ENDPOINTKEY = endpoints.ENDPOINTKEY.

relationships.description: Links an endpoint to its parent security system/application definition.
relationships.evidence: Saviynt documentation states that a security system can have one or more endpoints; the schema stores SECURITYSYSTEMKEY on endpoints and SYSTEMKEY on securitysystems.

relationships.description: Links an account-entitlement grant to the account receiving the access.
relationships.evidence: Observed directly in existing Saviynt analytics SQL: account_entitlements1.ACCOUNTKEY = accounts.ACCOUNTKEY.

relationships.description: Links an account-entitlement grant to the specific entitlement value assigned to the account.
relationships.evidence: Saviynt documentation identifies account_entitlements1 as storing assigned access and the schema contains ENTITLEMENT_VALUEKEY matching entitlement_values.ENTITLEMENT_VALUEKEY.

relationships.description: Links an individual entitlement value to the entitlement type/category it belongs to.
relationships.evidence: The entitlement value schema stores ENTITLEMENTTYPEKEY and entitlement_types uses ENTITLEMENTTYPEKEY as its primary key.

relationships.description: Links an entitlement type to the endpoint where that type of access is defined.
relationships.evidence: The entitlement type schema stores ENDPOINTKEY and endpoints uses ENDPOINTKEY as its primary key.

relationships.description: Links a role assignment record to the assigned Saviynt role.
relationships.evidence: role_user_account contains ROLEKEY and roles uses ROLEKEY as its primary key.

relationships.description: Links a role assignment record to the Saviynt user receiving the role.
relationships.evidence: role_user_account contains USERKEY and users uses USERKEY as its primary key.

relationships.description: Links a role assignment record to the account on which the role is represented or assigned.
relationships.evidence: role_user_account contains ACCOUNTKEY and accounts uses ACCOUNTKEY as its primary key.

relationships.description: Links a role-entitlement membership record to the role.
relationships.evidence: role_entitlements uses ROLEKEY in its composite primary key and roles uses ROLEKEY as its primary key.

relationships.description: Links a role-entitlement membership record to the entitlement contained in the role.
relationships.evidence: role_entitlements uses ENTITLEMENT_VALUEKEY in its composite primary key and entitlement_values uses ENTITLEMENT_VALUEKEY as its primary key.

relationships.description: Links a role hierarchy record to the parent role.
relationships.evidence: childroles stores PARENTROLEKEY and its documented purpose is parent/child role nesting.

relationships.description: Links a role hierarchy record to the child role.
relationships.evidence: childroles stores CHILDROLEKEY and its documented purpose is parent/child role nesting.

relationships.description: Links a customer-user association to the corresponding customer or organizational unit.
relationships.evidence: customer_users uses CUSTOMERKEY in its composite primary key and customer uses CUSTOMERKEY as its primary key.

relationships.description: Links a customer-user association to the corresponding Saviynt user.
relationships.evidence: customer_users uses USERKEY in its composite primary key and users uses USERKEY as its primary key.

relationships.description: Links a customer-endpoint association to the corresponding customer or organizational unit.
relationships.evidence: customer_endpoint uses CUSTOMERKEY in its composite primary key and customer uses CUSTOMERKEY as its primary key.

relationships.description: Links a customer-endpoint association to the endpoint scoped to that customer.
relationships.evidence: customer_endpoint stores ENDPOINTS as part of its composite primary key and the table purpose is to scope endpoints to a customer.

relationships.description: Links a customer-role association to the corresponding customer or organizational unit.
relationships.evidence: customer_roles uses CUSTOMERKEY in its composite primary key and customer uses CUSTOMERKEY as its primary key.

relationships.description: Links a customer-role association to the role scoped to that customer.
relationships.evidence: customer_roles uses ROLEKEY in its composite primary key and roles uses ROLEKEY as its primary key.

relationships.description: Links a customer-entitlement association to the corresponding customer or organizational unit.
relationships.evidence: customer_entitlementvalues uses CUSTOMERKEY in its composite primary key and customer uses CUSTOMERKEY as its primary key.

relationships.description: Links a customer-entitlement association to the entitlement value scoped to that customer.
relationships.evidence: customer_entitlementvalues stores ENTITLEMENT_VALUES and its documented purpose is to scope entitlement values to a customer.

relationships.description: Links a user-group membership record to the corresponding user group.
relationships.evidence: usergroup_users uses USER_GROUPKEY in its composite primary key and its documented purpose is user-group membership.

relationships.description: Links a user-group membership record to the Saviynt user who belongs to the group.
relationships.evidence: usergroup_users uses USERKEY in its composite primary key and users uses USERKEY as its primary key.

relationships.description: Links a user-group entitlement association to the corresponding user group.
relationships.evidence: usergroup_entitlements uses USER_GROUPKEY in its composite primary key and its documented purpose is to associate entitlements with user groups.

relationships.description: Links a user-group entitlement association to the entitlement value granted through the group.
relationships.evidence: usergroup_entitlements uses ENTITLEMENT_VALUEKEY in its composite primary key and entitlement_values uses ENTITLEMENT_VALUEKEY as its primary key.

relationships.description: Links a role ownership record to the role being owned.
relationships.evidence: role_owners uses ROLEKEY in its composite primary key and its documented purpose is role ownership.

relationships.description: Links a role ownership record to the Saviynt user who owns the role.
relationships.evidence: role_owners uses USERKEY in its composite primary key and users uses USERKEY as its primary key.

relationships.description: Links an entitlement ownership record to the entitlement value being owned.
relationships.evidence: entitlement_owners uses ENTITLEMENT_VALUEKEY in its composite primary key and its documented purpose is entitlement ownership.

relationships.description: Links an entitlement ownership record to the Saviynt user who owns the entitlement.
relationships.evidence: entitlement_owners uses USERKEY in its composite primary key and users uses USERKEY as its primary key.

relationships.description: Links an account ownership record to the account being owned.
relationships.evidence: accountowners stores ACCOUNTKEY and its documented purpose is account ownership.

relationships.description: Links an account ownership record to a user owner.
relationships.evidence: accountowners stores OWNERUSERKEY for user-based account ownership.

relationships.description: Links an access-request line item to its parent request header.
relationships.evidence: request_access stores REQUESTKEY and its documented purpose is to hold line items under an ARS request.

relationships.description: Links a provisioning task to the access request that produced or owns the task.
relationships.evidence: arstasks stores REQUESTKEY and ars_requests uses REQUESTKEY as its primary key.

relationships.description: Links a provisioning task to the specific request line item that generated the task.
relationships.evidence: arstasks stores REQUESTACCESSKEY and request_access uses REQUEST_ACCESSKEY as its primary key.

relationships.description: Links an approval-step record to the request line item being approved.
relationships.evidence: access_approvers stores REQUEST_ACCESS_KEY and its documented purpose is approval-step tracking for requests.
